# scripts/security-baseline.txt — findings that are KNOWN, not findings that
# are fine. Generated by scripts/security-scan.sh --update; do not hand-edit the
# comment block, it is regenerated from the script.
#
# Format: <tool>|<rule or advisory id>|<file or module>
# Line numbers are deliberately absent — a key that moves whenever anyone edits
# above it produces a baseline that gets regenerated without being read.
#
# What the initial sweep found, and why it is baselined rather than fixed
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# gosec, 93 keys. The HIGH ones were read individually:
#   G101 "hardcoded credentials" ×5 — all false: a SQL column list, an HTTP
#        header NAME, two error-code constants, and a default filename.
#   G404 "weak random" — retry-backoff jitter. Nothing that mints a
#        credential uses math/rand; sbtoken and the sandbox-id generator use
#        crypto/rand.
#   G115 "integer overflow on conversion" ×23 — the noisiest rule in gosec on
#        any Go codebase; kept in the baseline rather than excluded so a
#        conversion in a NEW file still surfaces.
#   G301/G302/G306 (permissions), G304 (file path from a variable) and G204
#        (subprocess from a variable) are the shape of this program: it makes
#        overlay files, opens tenant-named paths and runs the jailer.
#        internal/vm has its own path-confinement tests for the ones that
#        matter (3.6, 4.5).
#
# osv-scanner, 7 keys, 3 modules: logrus 1.8.1 (DoS via Entry.Writer),
#   mongo-driver 1.8.3 (OOB read in GSSAPI error handling) and chi 5.2.5
#   (three IP-spoofing advisories in middleware.RealIP). All three are
#   transitively required, none is called: `grep -r RealIP` over non-vendor Go
#   returns nothing, and govulncheck — which is call-graph aware — reports
#   "0 vulnerabilities called". They stay listed because osv-scanner's job is
#   to say "you are one call away", and that is worth knowing.
#
# govulncheck, 0 keys. Only CALLED findings are recorded here; that is the
#   whole reason it and osv-scanner are both wired.
#
# staticcheck, 2 keys, both cosmetic, both outside this change's scope.
#
# Adding a line is a decision. Say why, above it, in a comment.

# netns_linux.go's namespace build is in-process netlink since §2, but two
# child processes remain by design: one `nsenter --net=… nft -f -` per
# namespace for the atomic in-ns ruleset, and one host `nft -f -`
# (EnsureNetNSHostRules). Args are node-controlled (slot index, fixed device
# names), never tenant input — the same shape as storage.go below.
gosec|G204|internal/vm/netns_linux.go
# preflight.go's netns canary (add-sandbox-netns §3.2) runs `nsenter --net=<ns>
# nft list …` to read the KERNEL's view of the canary ruleset back — the whole
# point of the probe is not to trust this package's own strings. The path is
# /var/run/netns/ + a name this package composed from a constant prefix and a

# Added 2026-09-18 with add-named-snapshots. Both assessed, not waved through.
#
# G304 (file inclusion via variable) on the snapshot-export API. Every path it
# opens is <SnapshotDir>/<id>.ckpt/export-<build>/<name>, and none of the three
# parts is free text: `id` has passed s.owns() and names a sandbox the daemon
# holds, `build` has passed artifact.ValidateBuildID (letters, digits, - and _
# only, so it can carry neither "/" nor ".."), and the filename comes from a
# closed switch in exportObjectFile and never from the request at all. There is
# no input here that could traverse.
gosec|G304|internal/httpapi/snapshotexport.go
#
# G306 (WriteFile permissions) on /etc/hostname, written 0644. It has to be
# world-readable: every process in the guest that resolves the machine's name
# reads it, and 0600 would leave a non-root process unable to. This is the mode
# every distribution ships it with. The file is written by envd as root inside
# the sandbox, so the write itself is not a boundary crossing.
gosec|G306|cmd/envd/hostname.go

# Added 2026-09-19. Seven keys from four changes merged since the last Linux
# regeneration (99a3f79, 2026-09-01): add-sandbox-fork (internal/vm/fork.go,
# internal/vm/memsnap.go), add-sandbox-checkpoints (internal/vm/checkpoint.go,
# internal/sandbox/daemon/checkpoint.go) and add-sandbox-networks
# (internal/vm/tagnet_linux.go). Every file here was CREATED by one of those
# changes; none predates them. Grouped by rule, all three rules already
# documented above.
#
# G301 (directory permissions, 0755 rather than 0750) ×4. All four are the
# node's own scratch trees under OverlayDir/SnapshotDir, holding a checkpoint's
# state, memory image and overlay copy — the same shape as the 23 G301 keys
# above and the same 0755 the jailer chroot base is created with. Nothing in
# them is readable without also reaching the parent directories, which the node
# owns; no tenant process shares this filesystem. Tightening to 0750 changes a
# mode the fleet has always run 0755 for no measured gain.
gosec|G301|internal/sandbox/daemon/checkpoint.go
gosec|G301|internal/vm/checkpoint.go
gosec|G301|internal/vm/fork.go
gosec|G301|internal/vm/memsnap.go
#
# G304 (file inclusion via variable) ×2, same basis as the snapshotexport.go
# entry below: neither path has a free-text component.
#   internal/sandbox/daemon/checkpoint.go — readCheckpointMeta opens
#   <SnapshotDir>/<id>.ckpt/<name>/checkpoint.json. `id` has passed d.lookup()
#   and names a sandbox the daemon holds; `name` has passed
#   validCheckpointName (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$ — no "/", no "."), or comes
#   from os.ReadDir of that root, which is the filesystem's own listing rather
#   than request input.
#   internal/vm/memsnap.go — applyDiff opens the capture's diff and its
#   destination. Both are composed by the manager from lineageDir(sandboxID)
#   and fixed basenames; the request never names a file.
gosec|G304|internal/sandbox/daemon/checkpoint.go
gosec|G304|internal/vm/memsnap.go
#
# G204 (subprocess with variable arguments) on tagnet_linux.go's two iptables
# calls, which install one idempotent DOCKER-USER exception so slot-to-slot
# traffic is not vetoed before sandboxd_netns can judge it. The argv is the
# package-level constant dockerUserPeerRule plus a literal "-C"/"-I"; no value
# derived from a request reaches it. Same shape as the netns_linux.go and
# preflight.go entries above.
#
# G304 (file path from a variable) on rootfsdigest.go — digestOf opens the root
#   image a restore is about to boot. The path is either <SnapshotDir>/<template
#   name>/rootfs.squashfs, the same join the boot itself makes and with the name
#   already through ValidateTemplateName on the create path, or a fixed
#   rootfs.squashfs inside a capture directory the daemon composed. Neither is
#   request input, and the file is opened read-only to hash it.
gosec|G304|internal/vm/rootfsdigest.go
